UMR revises anti-amyloid coverage criteria for November

An October 1 UMR policy bulletin sets November 1 coverage criteria that align Leqembi and Kisunla with updated MRI/ARIA monitoring, require specialist oversight and biomarker-confirmed early Alzheimer disease, and add maintenance rules—including Kisunla amyloid-PET reassessment and Leqembi dosing expectations after 18 months.

Key label details: For Kisunla, initial coverage requires mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer dementia, positive amyloid PET, a baseline brain MRI within 12 months, no concurrent anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody and label-consistent dosing. The policy lists MMSE 20–30, MoCA 17–30 or SLUMS 17–30 in its medically necessary pathway and specifies MRI monitoring before the second, third, fourth and seventh infusions, with additional imaging as clinically indicated.

ManagementAmyloid PETDisease-modifying treatment eligibility

Added October 2, 2026 · UMR Medical Policy Update Bulletin, October 2026; effective 2026-11-01

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The update operationalizes eligibility, safety monitoring and long-term treatment rules rather than merely repeating drug labels. Both policies require MCI or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease, confirmed amyloid, recent baseline MRI and specialist oversight. The details differ: Kisunla coverage uses amyloid PET and adds ongoing PET-based continuation requirements; Leqembi allows specified CSF ratios or PET and defines expectations for monthly IV maintenance after 18 months while recognizing the self-administered subcutaneous product under the pharmacy benefit.

Study design

UMR's October 2026 Medical Policy Update Bulletin summarizes revised Leqembi and Kisunla medical-benefit coverage templates for UnitedHealthcare commercial and individual-exchange benefit plans. The policies specify initial and continuation criteria, biomarker confirmation, cognitive-stage thresholds, MRI schedules, counseling, specialist involvement, dosing and authorization duration. This is an access-policy action, not a clinical study or formal guideline.

Key label details

  • For Kisunla, initial coverage requires mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer dementia, positive amyloid PET, a baseline brain MRI within 12 months, no concurrent anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody and label-consistent dosing. The policy lists MMSE 20–30, MoCA 17–30 or SLUMS 17–30 in its medically necessary pathway and specifies MRI monitoring before the second, third, fourth and seventh infusions, with additional imaging as clinically indicated.
  • Kisunla continuation authorizations remain 12 months. Through 18 months, a positive baseline amyloid PET or a plan to obtain one by month 18 is required; after 18 months, the policy calls for at least annual post-treatment amyloid PET that remains positive, along with continued ARIA monitoring, specialist oversight and no other anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody.
  • For Leqembi, amyloid confirmation may use PET or specified CSF ratios. The policy recognizes IQLIK under the pharmacy benefit, and for intravenous maintenance after 18 months expects every-four-week dosing; continued every-two-week dosing requires prescriber attestation that transition is not clinically appropriate. Continuation MRI monitoring is listed after one, two, three and six months and as clinically indicated.

What changed

An October 1 payer bulletin announces November 1 operational coverage rules for updated anti-amyloid dosing, MRI safety monitoring, biomarker confirmation and continuation, including new distinctions between Leqembi formulations and maintenance schedules.

Strength of evidence

Authoritative evidence of the named payer's published policy change and effective date. The bulletin does not grade underlying clinical evidence, test outcomes or establish that these criteria are optimal; applicability depends on the member's specific plan and benefit administration.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Infusion and memory-clinic teams may need to adjust prior-authorization packets, MRI timing, biomarker documentation and long-term treatment plans before November 1. Label-compliant care does not by itself guarantee coverage when a plan imposes additional documentation or continuation requirements.

Field medical relevance

Directly relevant to anti-amyloid treatment access, patient counseling, prior authorization, specialty-pharmacy routing, ARIA monitoring and the distinction among FDA labeling, clinical guidance and payer coverage.

Access or reimbursement relevance

High. The update directly changes documentation, monitoring and continuation criteria for covered anti-amyloid therapy in affected plans, while leaving authorization, general availability and other payer policies unchanged.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Are these national Medicare criteria?
No. This is a UMR/UnitedHealthcare private-plan policy update. Medicare and other payers may use different rules, and the member's specific benefit plan controls.
Does the policy take effect immediately?
No. The bulletin was published October 1, 2026, and lists November 1, 2026, as the effective date for the identified policy changes.
Is the Kisunla annual amyloid PET requirement an FDA recommendation?
It is a payer continuation criterion described in this policy. Payer coverage criteria, FDA labeling and clinical-practice recommendations should be documented separately.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Policy applies only to identified UMR/UnitedHealthcare plan contexts
  • Benefit documents and member-specific plan terms supersede a general bulletin
  • Criteria become effective November 1 rather than on the October 1 publication date
  • Bulletin summarizes policy language and does not grade the clinical evidence base
  • Coverage approval does not establish comparative effectiveness or clinical utility
  • Other payers may use different biomarker, MRI, dosing and continuation requirements
